beats.html:
The panic was a story
about a story.

In 1938 Orson Welles read
War of the Worlds on the radio.

America supposedly lost
its mind. It did not.
The audience was small.

Newspapers were losing
advertising to radio, and had
every reason to make radio
look dangerous.

clip.match_reason: The fact is the 1938 War of the Worlds broadcast, and the plate is a 1938 cabinet radio with the dial lit warm and the armchair beside it empty, which is the small audience the fact is about.
